Definition: from the base of G3993; toil, i.e. (by implication) anguish:--pain.
BiblicalUsage: Ponos is toil that turns to anguish, pain that comes from labour. Paul says Epaphras has a great zeal for the churches, and the Greek behind it is labour, toil that costs the body. Revelation shows the other end of it: men gnawing their tongues for pain under judgment, and then the promise that in the new creation there shall be no more pain.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe pain is real and God does not pretend otherwise, and that is what makes the promise matter. The same God who lets his servants labour now will one day wipe away every tear and end the pain for good.
